title: Agentforce Alternatives in 2026: Options Compared
summary: Agentforce alternatives suit different platforms. Choose based on whether your agent works inside a CRM, office suite, service desk, or across apps.
body_markdown:
## Where Activepieces fits among Agentforce alternatives


When the agent has to work across several apps you already pay for, not inside Salesforce, Activepieces's the pick, with 741 integrations to work across.


It also suits you when you want the run bill to depend on what you build rather than on a per-conversation charge.


Under the hood, Activepieces's an open source automation platform with an AI agent step and an MIT-licensed core. That step can call the tools in its library of integrations, which it calls pieces, listed at[https://www.activepieces.com/integrations](https://www.activepieces.com/integrations) . Roughly 60% of those integrations are community-contributed.


### What it suits


Look first at the unit economics, because they are the reason to consider it. In an Agentforce-style model, each action the agent takes is a line item.


In a flow builder, the agent's one step among others, so you can see which steps are cheap deterministic work and which ones call a model. You spend model cost only where judgment is needed, and the rest of the flow stays plain automation.


In the screenshot, the Data Selector is open over a flow with a trigger and a selected code step, and the Variables tab lists a stored value named STRIPE_PROD.


Read it as an example of configuration living in one named place: a billing product identifier is set once and referenced by any step.


The code step's inputs therefore point to a variable instead of a pasted constant. That's how you keep a multi-app flow auditable when several people edit it.


Two other properties matter for buyers who care about control. The product documents approval steps, so a person can sign off before the agent writes to a customer record or sends a message.


The lock-in that hurts most when leaving Agentforce has nothing to do with how good your agent is: it runs only in Salesforce's cloud, so where it lives was settled before you built anything.


Activepieces treats deployment as a setting, and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production.


Managed cloud and self-hosted (Docker, Compose or Kubernetes) run one codebase, so a flow built on either can be moved to the other through Git Sync and Releases, which is in the docs.


RBAC, SSO, SCIM and audit logs are in both editions, so choosing where to run never costs you a control.


### What it does not do


It's not a Salesforce-native service agent. If the work's answering cases inside Service Cloud, grounded in Salesforce data models and permissions with no integration layer, Agentforce's built for exactly that.


Activepieces would reach Salesforce from outside, as one connection among many in a library of 741 integrations.


With Activepieces you also assemble and maintain the flows yourself, and flows are unlimited on every plan, including free, so the savings come with an engineering and monitoring duty that a bundled product absorbs for you.


Activepieces is the better fit for teams whose agents must work across several apps they already pay for, and who weigh exit freedom above all else.


Git Sync and Releases is a documented feature, and self-hosting via Docker, Compose or Kubernetes runs on the same codebase as the managed cloud, so where a flow runs never decides whether you can leave.


For buyers inside a Salesforce-centred stack, Agentforce keeps the tighter native fit, but on portability and on a bill that follows what you build rather than each action the agent takes, Activepieces comes out ahead.
